title: "Robustness-case_study-LOMO"
output: html_document

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(dplyr)
library(modelimportance)
library(here)
setwd(here())
```

We explore the robustness of model importance using the leave-one-model-out (LOMO) approach 
on the case study of 4-week ahead incident death forecasts in Massachusetts (MA).
We use forecasts from 9 models that submitted forecasts for the week of December 25, 2021.

In this case study, we exclude one model at a time from the set of all models, and calculate the importance scores of the remaining models.
For example, when we exclude the "CovidAnalytics-DELPHI" model, we calculate the importance scores of the remaining 8 models using the forecasts from these models only. We repeat this process for each of the 9 models.

## Load data

We load the forecast data and truth data for the specific prediction task, and 
convert them to the required format for the `model_importance()` function.

```{r}
forecasts_MA_2021 <- read.csv("../Data/forecasts_MA_2021_hor1-4.csv")
forecasts_MA_2021$target_end_date <- as.Date(forecasts_MA_2021$target_end_date)

# forecast data for MA, target_end_date = "2021-12-25", and
# for 4-week ahead incident death (horizon = 4)
models2include <- c(
  "CovidAnalytics-DELPHI", "USC-SI_kJalpha",
  "BPagano-RtDriven", "Karlen-pypm",
  "SteveMcConnell-CovidComplete", "UMass-MechBayes",
  "RobertWalraven-ESG", "COVIDhub-baseline",
  "UCSD_NEU-DeepGLEAM"
)
fdat <- forecasts_MA_2021 |>
  filter(
    model %in% models2include,
    location == "25",
    target_end_date == as.Date("2021-12-25"),
    horizon == 4
  ) |>
  mutate(
    forecast_date = as.Date("2021-11-28"),
    target = "wk inc death"
  ) |>
  rename(
    model_id = model,
    reference_date = forecast_date,
    output_type = type,
    output_type_id = quantile
  ) |>
  select(
    model_id, reference_date, location, horizon,
    target_end_date, target, output_type,
    output_type_id, value
  )

truth <- read.csv("../Data/truth_MA_2021.csv") |>
  select(target_end_date, location, value) |>
  mutate(
    target_end_date = as.Date(target_end_date),
    target = "wk inc death"
  ) |>
  rename(oracle_value = value)
```



## Calculate importance scores in LOMO approach

### Importance scores using all models as a reference
First, we calculate the importance scores using all models to have a reference.

```{r note, message=FALSE}
imp_ref <- model_importance(
  forecast_data = fdat,
  oracle_output_data = truth,
  ensemble_fun = "simple_ensemble",
  weighted = FALSE,
  importance_algorithm = "lomo",
  na_action = "worst"
) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), round, 3))

# NOTE:
# na_action does not need to be specified for this case study as no missing forecasts
# but, I included it as the mode_importance() function is not up to date yet.
# In the updated version, default setting is included, which will be merged soon.
```

### Calculate importance scores excluding one model from the set of models at a time

We exclude one model at a time from the set of all models, and calculate the importance scores of the remaining models.
The resulting output is stored in a data frame with columns `model_id, mean_importance, excluded_model` per each excluded model:

- `model_id`: the ID of the model whose importance score is calculated
- `mean_importance`: the importance score of the model. Since we have only one prediction task, this is the same as the importance score.
- `excluded_model`: the ID of the model that was excluded when calculating the importance score.

Note that the excluded model's importance metric is assigned as NA.

This process is repeated along all models, and the results are combined into a single data frame.

```{r}
models <- unique(fdat$model_id)

results_df <- furrr::future_map_dfr(
  models,
  function(m) {
    fdat_lomo <- fdat |> filter(model_id != m)

    res <- suppressMessages(
      model_importance(
        forecast_data = fdat_lomo,
        oracle_output_data = truth,
        ensemble_fun = "simple_ensemble",
        weighted = FALSE,
        importance_algorithm = "lomo",
        na_action = "worst"
      ) |>
        mutate(across(where(is.numeric), round, 3))
    ) |>
      right_join(fdat_temp, by = "model_id") |>
      arrange(model_id) |>
      mutate(excluded_model = m)

    res
  }
)
```


#### Summarize results

```{r}
results_df_summary <- results_df |>
  filter(!is.na(mean_importance)) |>
  group_by(model_id) |>
  summarize(
    avg_importance = mean(mean_importance, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_importance = sd(mean_importance, na.rm = TRUE),
    min_importance = min(mean_importance, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_importance = max(mean_importance, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
```

#### Visualize results

```{r}
library(ggplot2)


results_df |>
  filter(!is.na(mean_importance)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = model_id, y = mean_importance)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.55,
    outlier.shape = 1,
    outlier.size = 1
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = imp_ref,
    mapping = aes(x = model_id, y = mean_importance),
    shape = 23, fill = "black", size = 2,
    position = position_nudge(x = -0.4)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Model importance metric distributions",
    x = "Model",
    y = "Importance"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8, angle = 20, hjust = 0.85),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
    legend.position = "none",
    strip.text = element_text(size = 10)
  )
```

### Calculate importance scores across different subset sizes

```{r}
results_df <- list()
for (i in 2:9) {
  combo_list <- combn(models, i, simplify = FALSE)
  results_df[[i]] <- furrr::future_map_dfr(
    combo_list,
    function(combo) {
      fdat_lomo <- fdat |> filter(model_id %in% combo)

      res <- suppressMessages(
        model_importance(
          forecast_data = fdat_lomo,
          oracle_output_data = truth,
          ensemble_fun = "simple_ensemble",
          weighted = FALSE,
          importance_algorithm = "lomo",
          na_action = "worst"
        ) |>
          mutate(across(where(is.numeric), round, 3))
      ) |>
        right_join(fdat_temp, by = "model_id") |>
        arrange(model_id) |>
        mutate(
          subset_size = length(combo),
          included_models = paste(combo, collapse = ", ")
        )

      res
    }
  )
}

all_dfs <- dplyr::bind_rows(results_df)
```



```{r}
model_sorted <- all_dfs |> 
        filter(subset_size == 9) |> 
        arrange(desc(mean_importance)) |> 
        pull(model_id)


data2plot <- all_dfs |> 
  mutate(model_id = factor(model_id, levels = model_sorted)) |>
  filter(!is.na(mean_importance)) 

p <- data2plot |> filter(subset_size < 9) |> 
        ggplot(aes(x = factor(subset_size), y = mean_importance)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.55,
    outlier.shape = 1,
    outlier.size = 1
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ model_id, scales = "free_y") +
  geom_point(
    data = data2plot |> 
        filter(subset_size == 9),
    mapping = aes(x = factor(subset_size), y = mean_importance), size = 1) +
        labs(title = "Model importance metric distributions across different subset sizes",
             x = "Number of models in the subset",
             y = "Importance") + 
        theme(axis.text=element_text(size=8),
              axis.title=element_text(size=9),
              legend.position = "none",
              strip.text = element_text(size = 9))
        

pdf(file="imp_by_subsetsize.pdf",
    width = 8,
    height = 5)
p
dev.off()
```


















```{r anothor approach}
# Another approach: exclude more than one model at a time
models <- unique(fdat$model_id)

results_df2 <- list()
for (i in 1:7) {
  combo_list <- combn(models, i, simplify = FALSE)
  results_df2[[i]] <- furrr::future_map_dfr(
    combo_list,
    function(combo) {
      fdat_lomo <- fdat |> filter(!model_id %in% combo)

      res <- suppressMessages(
        model_importance(
          forecast_data = fdat_lomo,
          oracle_output_data = truth,
          ensemble_fun = "simple_ensemble",
          weighted = FALSE,
          importance_algorithm = "lomo",
          na_action = "worst"
        ) |>
          mutate(across(where(is.numeric), round, 3))
      ) |>
        right_join(fdat_temp, by = "model_id") |>
        arrange(model_id) |>
        mutate(
          num_excld_mod = length(combo),
          subset_size = 9 - length(combo),
          excluded_models = paste(combo, collapse = ", ")
        )

      res
    }
  )
}

all_dfs2 <- dplyr::bind_rows(results_df2)
```
